features: Native trace, quotient and randomization commitments observed in upstream order; resident alpha, zeta and next-row points.
Guarded commitment-prefix column selection feeds native quotient evaluation without private host readback.
Native PCS rounds in random, trace, quotient order; final openings moved into the standard proof type.

Unchanged CPU verification rejects altered public inputs, trace openings and degree metadata without executing CUDA.

Errors after trace, quotient and PCS, unwind, and real late PCS output-admission failure retire every randomness family and release intermediates.

admission.trace_log_rows: 1..24, further bounded by extended height plus production blowup <=25
admission.host: Public compilation uses existing bounded symbolic admission. Caps and assembly metadata reserve space before PCS output admission.
admission.device: Primitive and retained-prefix admission remains active at every stage; late failures are guarded across the complete attempt.

limitations: Native single-AIR proving from resident trace/public inputs; wallet request witness/public generation is not yet routed through CUDA.
The cubic test uses the recursive field profile, not a recursive machine AIR or batch proof.
Recursive lookup/batch orchestration, stage receipts, backend selection, whole-request worker admission and pool integration remain unfinished.
Correctness and resource qualification only; no full-request CUDA or transaction-throughput measurement.
CUDA execution is qualified only on the desktop RTX 5080. Volta has target compilation coverage; V100 execution, Metal execution and multiple GPUs remain untested.
Deterministic seeds are test-only. Exact byte comparisons disable PoW; production-parameter cases retain the normal PoW and CPU verification.
The intentional missing-kernel test runs outside sanitizers. All five opt-in primitive benchmarks are excluded from correctness and sanitizer runs.
qualification_note: Focused development checks passed, including the added real late PCS host-admission failure. The first qualification passed all CUDA and sanitizer checks, then the OpenCL build exposed two shared periodic fields whose visibility had not moved with their consumer. The visibility correction is included in the final frozen-source rerun; the initial build failure is preserved in attempt-01. Frozen-source qualification also re-runs the existing OpenCL periodic expansion and wallet batch test after extracting the shared periodic geometry. GPU checks run serially under 3 GiB RAM, zero swap, four CPU cores and 96 tasks. The stream build has 6 GiB and one build job.
